backlog.title: PRD Compliance Bug Fixes
backlog.description: Fix all 7 validated behavioral/PRD-compliance deviations (3 Major, 4 Minor) in the pi-mulligan extension. None are crashes or data-loss bugs — hidden content always remains on disk (soft-delete guarantee holds). The fixes restore spec compliance for the drift-nudge suppression mechanism (BUG-001), the pinned-hide permanence guarantee post-compaction (BUG-002), the drift-nudge acceptance criteria (BUG-003), and four minor polish items (BUG-004 through BUG-007).

milestones.title: Major Bug Fixes (BUG-001, BUG-002, BUG-003)
milestones.description: The three Major-severity bugs that significantly impact core functionality: (1) the drift nudge is wrongly suppressed for ~10 minutes after any rewind/shrink via a wall-clock window instead of the spec's turn-based check; (2) pinned rewinds stop working entirely after the first compaction, leaking hidden content back into the model's view; (3) the drift nudge does not fire for 'three ~4k turns in a row', violating spec §5.1 acceptance criterion (b).

tasks.title: BUG-001: Replace wall-clock suppressCheck with turn-based lower bound
tasks.description: spec/07 §5.3 (REQUIRED hard rule) says the per-turn drift nudge MUST NOT fire only 'for a turn in which the agent already issued a mulligan:rewind or mulligan:shrink'. The mechanism must be turn-based: a marker is 'during the metric's turn' iff it was created between the previous turn_end (previous metric's ts) and the current metric's ts. The implementation uses a fixed 10-minute wall-clock window (NUDGE_TURN_WINDOW_MS = 10*60*1000) which over-suppresses for ~10 minutes after ANY rewind/shrink. The data needed for the correct turn-based lower bound (recentMetrics) is now available via readMarkers but unused by suppressCheck.

subtasks.title: Refactor suppressCheck to use recentMetrics turn-boundary as lower bound
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_5b685875f3df/bugfix/001_f8322783910c/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-001. suppressCheck (src/nudges.ts:397-411) currently takes (metric: TurnMetric, markers: {rewinds, shrinks}) and suppresses iff some marker.ts falls in (metric.ts − 10min, metric.ts]. The correct behavior per spec/07 §5.3: suppress iff some marker.ts falls in (prevMetric.ts, metric.ts] where prevMetric is the SECOND-newest metric. readMarkers (src/markers.ts) returns recentMetrics: TurnMetric[] sorted NEWEST-FIRST (recentMetrics[0] = latest, recentMetrics[1] = previous). The markers param's ts is Date.now() stamped by appendRewindMarker/appendShrinkMarker. The metric's ts is stamped by appendTurnMetric.
2. INPUT: metric (TurnMetric — the latest, recentMetrics[0]), recentMetrics (TurnMetric[] — full array newest-first), markers ({rewinds: ReadonlyArray<RewindMarker>, shrinks: ReadonlyArray<ShrinkMarker>} — same as current).
3. LOGIC: Change suppressCheck signature to suppressCheck(metric: TurnMetric, recentMetrics: TurnMetric[], markers: {rewinds, shrinks}). Compute the turn-boundary lower bound: if recentMetrics.length >= 2, lo = recentMetrics[1].ts (the previous metric's ts); else (first turn / only one metric), lo = 0 (or suppress based on marker.ts <= metric.ts — on the first turn, any marker with ts <= metric.ts WAS created during this turn, so suppress). For each marker in rewinds + shrinks: suppress (return true) iff marker.ts > lo AND marker.ts <= metric.ts (both ts read defensively: non-finite → NaN → not in window → no suppress). Remove or deprecate the NUDGE_TURN_WINDOW_MS constant (line 270) and its export — it is no longer used. The existing defensive ts handling (typeof === number && Number.isFinite) stays.
4. OUTPUT: boolean — true iff some marker was created during the metric's turn (turn-boundary to turn_end). The filter.ts call site composes this as: fire = shouldNudge(...) && !suppressCheck(metric, recentMetrics, markers).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on suppressCheck to document the turn-based lower bound mechanism, the recentMetrics parameter, and why the previous wall-clock window was replaced. Remove the stale 'no per-turn lower bound' justification from the WHY-a-window comment.

tasks.title: BUG-002: Make resolvePinnedHide/resolvePinnedShrink compaction-aware
tasks.description: After the first compaction in a session, resolvePinnedHide bails entirely (returns []) because entryMessageYield returns -1 for compaction entries. This makes EVERY pinned rewind a permanent no-op, leaking previously-hidden content back into the model's view — violating PRD success criterion #1. The same bug affects resolvePinnedShrink. The fix uses a retained-tail-only walk: find the LAST compaction entry on the branch, walk only entries AFTER it (which map 1:1 to the tail of event.messages), and match pinned entry IDs there.

subtasks.title: Rewrite resolvePinnedHide to use retained-tail walk (compaction-aware)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_5b685875f3df/bugfix/001_f8322783910c/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-002 and external_deps.md (getBranch vs event.messages distinction). resolvePinnedHide (src/transforms.ts:625-660) currently filters branchEntries to isContextProducingType (which INCLUDES compaction), walks forward via entryMessageYield, and returns [] the instant it hits a compaction entry (yield -1). isContextProducingType (transforms.ts:555) returns true for {message, custom_message, branch_summary, compaction}. entryMessageYield (transforms.ts:549) returns 1 for {message, custom_message, branch_summary} and -1 for everything else. The key insight: entries AFTER the last compaction on the branch are the 'retained tail' and each (type message/custom_message/branch_summary) maps to exactly 1 message in event.messages. The retained tail maps to the LAST tailEntries.length messages.
2. INPUT: messages (MessageLike[] — compaction-aware, what the model sees), branchEntries (BranchEntry[] — root→leaf raw path from getBranch()), hideEntryIds (string[] — stable entry IDs pinned at marker creation). All unchanged from the current signature.
3. LOGIC: Replace the forward-walk algorithm with a retained-tail walk:
  (a) Defensive checks stay the same (non-array → [], empty hideEntryIds → [], build hideSet).
  (b) Find lastCompactionIdx = index of the LAST entry on branchEntries with type === 'compaction' (scan from end; -1 if none).
  (c) tailEntries = branchEntries.slice(lastCompactionIdx + 1).filter(e => type is 'message' | 'custom_message' | 'branch_summary'). Do NOT include 'compaction' (we are past it). Do NOT include 'label'/'custom' (not context-producing).
  (d) tailStartIdx = messages.length - tailEntries.length. If tailStartIdx < 0 → return [] (alignment lost — defensive).
  (e) Walk tailEntries forward: for entry at position k, msgIdx = tailStartIdx + k. If entry.id (string, via readOwn) ∈ hideSet → push msgIdx to remove.
  (f) Return remove (ascending by construction). When lastCompactionIdx === -1 (no compaction), this degenerates to walking ALL context-producing entries (excluding compaction), tailStartIdx = messages.length - allEntries.length = 0 — identical to the current no-compaction behavior.
  DO NOT change entryMessageYield or isContextProducingType (resolveCheckpoint still needs the bail-on-compaction behavior for its contiguous-sweep semantics). DO NOT change the function signature or return type (still number[], never null). The filterPipeline call site (transforms.ts:1065) passes resolvePinnedHide(messages, branch, hideEntryIds) — unchanged.
4. OUTPUT: number[] — ascending message indices to hide. Non-empty when pinned entries are in the retained tail (the production case post-compaction). Empty when pinned entries are in the compacted-away head (correct — they're gone from messages) or on defensive failures.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Rewrite the JSDoc on resolvePinnedHide to document the retained-tail walk algorithm, explaining why compaction no longer causes a total bail, and that entries in the compacted head are correctly unmatched (they're absent from messages). Reference spec/08 E24.

subtasks.title: Apply compaction-aware retained-tail walk to resolvePinnedShrink
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_5b685875f3df/bugfix/001_f8322783910c/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-002. resolvePinnedShrink (src/transforms.ts:813-842) has the IDENTICAL compaction-bail bug as resolvePinnedHide: it filters to isContextProducingType (includes compaction), walks forward via entryMessageYield, and returns null when it hits a compaction entry (yield -1). This makes pinned shrinks no-op post-compaction too — the PRD focuses on pinned rewinds (BUG-002) but the shrink resolver has the same root cause and must be fixed for consistency.
2. INPUT: messages (MessageLike[]), branchEntries (BranchEntry[]), pinnedEntryId (string). Unchanged signature.
3. LOGIC: Apply the SAME retained-tail walk algorithm from P1.M1.T2.S1, adapted for a single-ID lookup instead of a set:
  (a) Defensive checks stay the same.
  (b) Find lastCompactionIdx (same as S1).
  (c) tailEntries = slice after last compaction, filter to message/custom_message/branch_summary.
  (d) tailStartIdx = messages.length - tailEntries.length. If < 0 → return null.
  (e) Walk tailEntries: for entry at position k, if entry.id === pinnedEntryId → return tailStartIdx + k (the FIRST match — there is at most one since entry IDs are unique).
  (f) Return null if not found in the retained tail (correct — the pinned entry was compacted away; identity-or-nothing, matching the rewind precedent).
  The filterPipeline pinned-shrink path (transforms.ts:1135: resolvePinnedShrink(messages, branch, pinnedId)) and applyShrink's internal call (transforms.ts:855) are unchanged — they already handle null correctly (no-op).
4. OUTPUT: number | null — the message index of the pinned entry in the retained tail, or null when absent/compacted-away/alignment-lost.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on resolvePinnedShrink to document the retained-tail walk and why compaction no longer causes a no-op for retained-tail targets.

tasks.title: BUG-003: Make shouldNudge satisfy §5.1 acceptance criterion (b)
tasks.description: shouldNudge uses a moving-average compared strictly > to driftThresholdTokens (6000). avg([4000,4000,4000]) = 4000 < 6000 → does not fire, violating spec §5.1 acceptance criterion (b) 'three ~4k turns in a row DO fire'. The fix lowers the default threshold to 4000 and changes the comparison from > to >= so that three ~4k turns (avg 4000 >= 4000) fire while a single 8k turn amid small turns (avg 3000 < 4000) does not.

subtasks.title: Lower driftThresholdTokens default to 4000 and change shouldNudge comparison to >=
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_5b685875f3df/bugfix/001_f8322783910c/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-003. shouldNudge (src/nudges.ts:326-334) computes avg(window deltas) and compares strictly > driftThresholdTokens. DEFAULT_CONFIG.nudges.driftThresholdTokens = 6000 (src/config.ts). Verification of the fix: (a) avg([8000,500,500])=3000 >= 4000? No ✓; (b) avg([4000,4000,4000])=4000 >= 4000? Yes ✓; (c) avg(~0) >= 4000? No ✓. The drift_nudge.test.ts test helper cfg(windowTurns=3, threshold=6000) passes an EXPLICIT threshold, so lowering the DEFAULT_CONFIG value will NOT break existing tests that use cfg(). Audit test files for any test that reads DEFAULT_CONFIG.nudges.driftThresholdTokens directly instead of passing an explicit value.
2. INPUT: recentMetrics (TurnMetric[]), config (MulliganConfig). Unchanged signature.
3. LOGIC: (a) In src/config.ts DEFAULT_CONFIG, change nudges.driftThresholdTokens from 6000 to 4000. Update the JSDoc comment on driftThresholdTokens to explain: 'Default 4000. The moving-average over driftWindowTurns (default 3) compared with >= satisfies all three §5.1 acceptance criteria: (a) a single 8k turn amid small turns averages <4000 → no fire; (b) three ~4k turns average ~4000 >= 4000 → fire; (c) a single large result with ~0 net growth averages ~0 → no fire.' (b) In src/nudges.ts shouldNudge, change the return from `avg > config.nudges.driftThresholdTokens` to `avg >= config.nudges.driftThresholdTokens`. (c) Update the SPEC-AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION comment in shouldNudge to note that criterion (b) is now satisfied with the lowered threshold and >= comparison, removing the 'ILLUSTRATIVE' recharacterization.
4. OUTPUT: boolean — true iff avg(window deltas) >= driftThresholdTokens (delta-only when delta data exists); bloatHit fallback unchanged.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on driftThresholdTokens in config.ts (new default + rationale) and the shouldNudge SPEC-AMBIGUITY RESOLUTION comment in nudges.ts. These ride WITH the work.

milestones.title: Minor Bug Fixes (BUG-004 through BUG-007)
milestones.description: Four minor-severity polish items: (1) pendingBloatHits memory leak when perTurnDrift=false; (2) retry budget counting cancelled rewinds; (3) cancel no-op text mismatch on the target path; (4) checkpoint tool not gated by config.enabled. Each is a small, self-contained fix.

tasks.title: BUG-004: Fix pendingBloatHits unbounded accumulation when perTurnDrift=false
tasks.description: turnEndMetricHandler clears rt.pendingBloatHits at line 218, AFTER the perTurnDrift early-return at line 200. When bloatReminder=true but perTurnDrift=false, the clear never runs and pendingBloatHits grows by one entry per bloated result for the entire session.

subtasks.title: Move pendingBloatHits clear before the perTurnDrift early-return
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_5b685875f3df/bugfix/001_f8322783910c/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-004. turnEndMetricHandler (src/nudges.ts:188-220) has the structure: read sessionId → getConfig() → early-return if !enabled || !perTurnDrift (line 200) → ... → rt.pendingBloatHits = [] (line 218). bloatReminderHandler (src/nudges.ts:130-145) pushes to rt.pendingBloatHits unconditionally (its own gate is bloatReminder, not perTurnDrift). The clear at line 218 snapshots pendingBloatHits into the metric's bloatHits field AND resets it — both must happen only when perTurnDrift is on (the metric is only persisted when perTurnDrift is on). The FIX: move ONLY the reset (rt.pendingBloatHits = []) to before the early-return, while keeping the snapshot+bloat metric logic where it is. Specifically: after `const rt = getRuntime(sessionId)` and before the `if (!config.enabled || !config.nudges.perTurnDrift) return;` gate, add `rt.pendingBloatHits = [];` so the accumulator is always cleared every turn_end regardless of the perTurnDrift flag. When perTurnDrift IS on, the existing line 218 still snapshots the (now-already-cleared, but re-populated if a bloat result arrived between the clear and line 218 — impossible since tool_result fires before turn_end) array. Actually, since tool_result fires BEFORE turn_end within the same turn, and the clear runs at the TOP of turn_end, the snapshot at line 218 would see an empty array. FIX: move the snapshot+clear as a block to BEFORE the gate — `const bloat = rt.pendingBloatHits; rt.pendingBloatHits = [];` — and pass `bloat` into the metric. Then the gate runs after. This way bloat is always cleared (BUG-004 fix) AND the snapshot is correct when perTurnDrift is on.
2. INPUT: rt (SessionRuntime — from getRuntime(sessionId)), config (MulliganConfig).
3. LOGIC: Move lines 215-218 (the `const bloat = rt.pendingBloatHits; rt.pendingBloatHits = [];` block) from AFTER the perTurnDrift gate to BEFORE it (right after `const rt = getRuntime(sessionId)` on the line after line 196). The `bloat` const is then referenced later when building the metric (only reached when perTurnDrift is on). The metric's bloatHit/bloatHits fields use the captured `bloat` variable.
4. OUTPUT: rt.pendingBloatHits is always cleared at every turn_end, preventing unbounded growth. The metric snapshot is unchanged when perTurnDrift is on.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on turnEndMetricHandler to note that pendingBloatHits is cleared before the perTurnDrift gate (always cleared, not just when perTurnDrift is on).

tasks.title: BUG-005: Exclude cancelled rewinds from the per-prompt retry budget
tasks.description: countRetriesAtLatestPrompt counts every mulligan:rewind entry after the latest user prompt, with no exclusion for rewinds retired by a later mulligan:cancel. A cancelled rewind never took effect but still consumes budget.

subtasks.title: Make countRetriesAtLatestPrompt cancel-aware (subtract cancelled rewinds)
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_5b685875f3df/bugfix/001_f8322783910c/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-005. countRetriesAtLatestPrompt (src/tools/rewind.ts:247-281) finds the last user-prompt entry, then counts entries after it where type === 'custom' && customType === 'mulligan:rewind'. A mulligan:cancel entry has type === 'custom', customType === 'mulligan:cancel', and data.targetId === the cancelled marker's uuid (data.id). readMarkers (src/markers.ts / src/filter.ts:120-204) builds cancelledIds the same way: scans for mulligan:cancel entries, reads data.targetId, drops markers whose data.id ∈ that set. The rewind marker's uuid is in entry.data.id.
2. INPUT: ctx (ExtensionContext — sessionManager.getEntries() FRESH).
3. LOGIC: In countRetriesAtLatestPrompt, after the existing rewind-count loop, ALSO scan the same entries (after latestPromptIndex) for mulligan:cancel entries. For each cancel entry, read data.targetId. Then re-scan the counted rewind entries: for each counted rewind, read its data.id; if that id matches any cancel's targetId, subtract it from the count. Implementation approach: (a) Build a Set<string> cancelledRewindIds from all mulligan:cancel entries after latestPromptIndex (read data.targetId via defensive access). (b) In the rewind-counting loop, for each mulligan:rewind entry, read its data.id; if data.id ∈ cancelledRewindIds, do NOT increment count (skip it). This is cleaner than subtract-after-counting. Read data.id and data.targetId defensively (try/catch per entry, mirroring the existing Proxy-safe pattern). The OVER-APPROXIMATION comment should be updated to note that cancelled rewinds are now excluded.
4. OUTPUT: number — count of ACTIVE (non-cancelled) mulligan:rewind entries after the latest user prompt. Never throws (E13).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the JSDoc on countRetriesAtLatestPrompt to document the cancel-exclusion logic.

tasks.title: BUG-006: Split cancel no-op text by resolution path (target vs markerId)
tasks.description: cancel.ts:393 returns a single hardcoded string 'Mulligan: no active marker found with that id — nothing to cancel.' for BOTH the target-not-found and markerId-not-found cases. spec/05 §5 specifies two distinct texts.

subtasks.title: Emit spec-correct no-op text for target vs markerId resolution paths
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_5b685875f3df/bugfix/001_f8322783910c/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-006. cancelExecute (src/tools/cancel.ts) resolves the marker via two paths: (3a) MARKERID PATH — when params.markerId is a non-empty string (scans entries for matching customType mulligan:rewind/shrink with id === markerId); (3b) TARGET PATH — when params.target is set (resolveTargetUuid resolves the target to a covering marker). If neither path yields a targetUuid, step 4 (cancel.ts:393) returns the not-found no-op. The current code returns ONE hardcoded string regardless of which path was attempted. The existing test at test/tools/cancel.test.ts:560 pins this unified string and must be updated.
2. INPUT: params (the cancel tool params — has optional markerId?: string and optional target?: ShrinkTarget-like). The resolution already happened in steps 3a/3b.
3. LOGIC: Before the `if (targetUuid === null)` check at cancel.ts:392, determine which path was attempted: `const usedMarkerId = typeof params.markerId === 'string' && params.markerId.length > 0;`. In the not-found block, emit: if usedMarkerId → 'Mulligan: no active marker found with that id — nothing to cancel.' (unchanged); else (target path or neither) → 'Mulligan: no active marker found for that target — nothing to cancel.' (the spec/05 §5 verbatim target-path text). The details stay { cancelled: false }.
4. OUTPUT: The correct no-op text per the resolution path. No behavior change beyond the text.
5. DOCS: none — tool result text is not externally documented (it's agent-facing runtime text, not a config/API surface). The existing cancel.test.ts:560 test that pins the unified string must be updated to assert the correct path-specific text.

tasks.title: BUG-007: Add config.enabled gate to mulligan_checkpoint
tasks.description: checkpoint.ts performs no config.enabled check, so with the extension disabled it still writes mulligan:checkpoint labels. Spec E14 requires all tools to refuse with 'Mulligan is disabled.' when config.enabled === false.

subtasks.title: Add getConfig().enabled gate to checkpointExecute
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/006_5b685875f3df/bugfix/001_f8322783910c/architecture/system_context.md §BUG-007. checkpointExecute (src/tools/checkpoint.ts:96-130) has NO config.enabled check. The other four tools all gate on it: src/tools/rewind.ts has `if (!getConfig().enabled) return refusal(...)` at the top of execute; cancel.ts:356 has `if (!getConfig().enabled) return refusal('Mulligan is disabled')`. The checkpoint tool already imports getConfig indirectly — it imports from markers.ts but NOT config.ts. ADD the import: `import { getConfig } from '../config.js';`. The refusal() helper (checkpoint.ts:84-89) builds `{ content: [{type:'text', text: 'Mulligan: refused — <reason>'}], details: { name } }`. The existing refusal format prefixes with 'Mulligan: refused — ' but E14 says tools should say 'Mulligan is disabled.' — match the other tools' exact text. Check how the other tools phrase it: cancel.ts:356 uses a literal `return { content: [...], details: {...} }` not the refusal() helper — verify the exact text pattern used by rewind/cancel/audit for the disabled case and match it.
2. INPUT: none beyond the existing params (name, ctx, pi).
3. LOGIC: At the top of checkpointExecute's try block (after `const name = params?.name;`), add: `if (!getConfig().enabled) { return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: 'Mulligan: disabled.' }], details: { name: typeof name === 'string' ? name : '' } }; }`. Match the exact disabled-text pattern used by the other four tools (verify by grepping `getConfig().enabled` in src/tools/*.ts — use the same wording). Add the import `import { getConfig } from '../config.js';` at the top of checkpoint.ts.
4. OUTPUT: When config.enabled === false, checkpointExecute returns a disabled-refusal text result and does NOT call setCheckpoint (no label written). All other behavior unchanged.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] Update the checkpoint.ts file header comment that currently says 'NO config gate here (GOTCHA #4)' — replace with documentation that the config.enabled gate is now present per spec E14, and checkpoints respect the master switch like all other tools.
